kind: repair campaign (FRETISH + TLSF), two-arm, paired -- replication of 2026-08-20-ops-grammar under the pending weakening default
kind_note: An exact mirror of ops-grammar apart from run_weakening = false, so the two campaigns' rows assemble into a grammar x weakening 2x2 on identical (spec, seed) pairs. Verified rather than assumed: across a matched pair of runs, exactly one of the 41 effective config keys in run.json differs, filters.run_weakening.
question: Whether the seven grammar repairs of 2026-08-19 improve repair quality under the weakening default counter is moving to, rather than the one every archived campaign ran. ops-grammar/PLAN.md section 8 registered this campaign before either ran: the screen 'caps both arms, and the cap is not small ... Removing it therefore raises headroom on both arms, and plausibly not symmetrically, the treatment arm having produced 76% more gate-passing candidates for the screen to discard.'
endpoint: Paired per-run implies_ideal, exact McNemar over the discordant pairs, per path, never pooled. The same endpoint and the same decision rule as ops-grammar, which is the plan this campaign is scored against; it has no separate PLAN.md.

tlsf.verdict: no significant difference; exactly 15 discordant pairs each way

result.found_repair_note: Yield is 100% on both arms and both paths, against 96.7-98.8% under the screen. With the weakening screen off, no run in the campaign failed to emit a repair.

decision_rule_firing: Outcome 3 as written: no significant difference on either path, so the repairs stay behind the key and REPORT.md's claim is downgraded. This is the firing under the configuration ops-grammar/PLAN.md section 8 named as the one that decides what ships.
decision: The maintainer decided otherwise on 2026-08-20, and the divergence is recorded rather than smoothed over. genetic.repaired_operators was removed and the repaired grammar made unconditional, on the strength of ops-grammar's outcome-1 firing under the screen-on configuration, minepump's reachability result, and the 2026-08-14 audit. The pre-registered rule, read under the configuration it named, says do not flip. Both readings are in the archive so the disagreement stays checkable; see ops-grammar/PROVENANCE.json for the same statement from the other side.
pooled_null_is_heterogeneous: The TLSF null is 15 discordant pairs each way, and that is not an absence of effect everywhere. It is minepump at 8-2 and codesample-un2 at 2-0 cancelling against humanoid-531 at 3-9, with codesample-un1 and gyro-var2 contributing one each to the control side. minepump is 0/20 under opslegacy with the screen on, 7/20 with it off, and 12/20 and 13/20 respectively under opsfixed -- so removing the screen recovers 7 of the 12 runs the repaired grammar reached, and the repaired grammar still leads 13 to 7 at a sample 20 seeds cannot resolve. humanoid-531 is the family the pilot measured building much larger formulae under the treatment arm, 630.4 s against 390.4 s, and it loses runs in both campaigns. The plan registered no per-spec test; these figures are exploratory and are recorded because reporting only the pooled sum would hide that the families pull in both directions.

two_by_two.note: Assembled on the (spec, seed) cases both campaigns ran: 120 FRETISH and 240 TLSF. The weakening contrast down each column is BETWEEN campaigns rather than within one, so it is unrandomised and descriptive. It is not confounded by a code change: 201d925..09a5eb8 touches only scripts/ and experiments/, no file under src/, include/, cmake/ or CMakeLists.txt, so the two campaigns ran behaviourally identical binaries.

screen_off_vs_on_paired.note: Counts, not p-values, and deliberately so. run_weakening_filter is a FINAL screen over the realizable survivors that draws nothing from the RandomSource, so both campaigns' matched runs search identically and turning it off can essentially only admit repairs -- the direction is near-structural rather than discovered, and a two-sided McNemar would overstate the evidence by testing a one-sided quantity. The magnitude is the finding. Confirmed from the data: best_fitness in the results CSV is derived by parse_repair_files() from the emitted repair files rather than from the population, so it is an output statistic and its differing between campaigns is what a final screen does, not evidence of a different search.
screen_off_vs_on_paired.not_a_strict_superset: In 27 of the 720 matched runs (22 TLSF, 5 FRETISH) n_repairs FELL with the screen off. The implication filter runs after the weakening screen and keeps only maximal specs, so admitting more candidates lets a newly admitted non-weakening dominate and displace several weakenings. Losing implies_ideal is therefore possible in principle; it happened in 0 of 720.

two_by_two.interaction: The grammar effect is +13 TLSF runs with the screen on and 0 with it off; +6 FRETISH runs with it on and +1 with it off. The two changes recover substantially the same repairs, which is why the effect ops-grammar measured does not survive the default it was measured against moving.
two_by_two.screen_evidence: Strictly one-way in every cell, and no run anywhere lost implies_ideal when the screen came off -- 0 of 720. This is the largest measurement yet of what the weakening screen forecloses, against 2026-08-19-weakening-arbiter's 9 of 120 paired repairs, and it is what run_weakening_filter's flip to false on 2026-08-20 rests on. Read it as a magnitude rather than as a significance test, for the reason screen_off_vs_on_paired.note gives.

profile_commit.subject: feat(experiments): add ops-weakening, the run_weakening = false replication
profile_commit.held_by_tag_note:
LOAD-BEARING, AND UNDER THE NEVER-DELETE RULE. The branch fix/mutation-operators was squashed on 2026-08-20, so d730c27, 201d925 and 09a5eb8 are not ancestors of the history that reaches main and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 201d925 main` will not succeed. The annotated tag provenance/mutation-operators, together with the campaign/ops-weakening branch, is what keeps them and every blob sha this file names resolvable against git gc. Push the tag and do not delete it; this is the position 2026-07-31-replicate and the TLSF branch are in.

What the squash does NOT cost is the substantive claim, because this file does not rest on the shas alone. `engine_tree` above names the compiled source by content, and those tree ids are identical across all three commits and are carried by the archival commit itself, which sits before the commit that removed genetic.repaired_operators and rewrote src/ and include/. So 'this binary was built from this source' stays verifiable from main's own history even if every sha below stops resolving. The shas remain recorded because they are what the binaries reported -- 720 rows carry them in the CSV `commit` column -- and are data about the run rather than pointers this archive depends on.
profile_commit.reachable_from_main_note: False and expected to stay false: the branch was squashed rather than merged, so the content reaches main under a fresh sha. Verify the engine instead of the commit, with `git rev-parse <commit>:src` against the engine_tree ids above.

merge_disposition.why: Chosen deliberately once engine_tree made the provenance claim content-addressed rather than sha-addressed. The ordering constraint the squash had to respect is that the archival commit stays separate from, and before, the commit removing genetic.repaired_operators, so that a commit carrying the campaigns' engine tree remains reachable from main.

profile_commit_evidence: Both hosts were staged through campaign.py, which fetches the pushed commit, checks it out, rebuilds and reads counter --version back before anything launches. Each per-host manifest records git.head and both binaries at that commit with dirty 0. --allow-stale-binary was never passed to a run that produced a retained row.

engine_tree.note:
The engine the campaign ran, named by content rather than by commit. These git tree and blob ids are identical across all three of d730c27 (ops-pilot), 201d925 (ops-grammar) and 09a5eb8 (ops-weakening): the commits differ only under experiments/ and scripts/, so one compiled source tree produced every binary in all three campaigns, and the binaries differ from each other solely in the version string cmake/version.cmake bakes in. Verify with `git rev-parse <commit>:src` and so on.

This is the durable half of the provenance and it is why the recorded commit shas may be rewritten. A squash or rebase replays content under fresh shas, but a tree id is content-addressed and does not move, so the claim 'this binary was built from this source' survives intact provided some commit reachable from main still carries these ids. The one requirement a rewrite must respect is therefore that the archival commits stay SEPARATE from, and ordered before, the commit that removed genetic.repaired_operators -- that removal changes src/ and include/, so a history in which it is squashed together with the archive leaves no commit carrying the tree these campaigns ran, and the ids below would name objects git gc collects. Kept apart, the tag provenance/mutation-operators is redundant and may be deleted.

binary_commit.source: counter --version, captured on both hosts into the per-host manifests after the pre-launch rebuild

known_caveats: Sweep O and the opswk-fret / opswk-tlsf profiles are retired with genetic.repaired_operators, removed on 2026-08-20. Every config in this archive sets that key, so none of them runs against a current binary. Reproduce at 09a5eb8 through the vendored scripts/.

A null bounds the effect below what 240 TLSF and 120 FRETISH pairs resolve. It is not evidence of no effect, and the per-spec breakdown above shows it is a sum of families pulling both ways rather than a flat zero.

The weakening contrast in the 2x2 is between two campaigns rather than within one. The binaries are behaviourally identical and both arms of every grammar pair ran on one host, but seeds were not re-randomised across the weakening factor and the two campaigns ran at different times of day on shared machines.
The simplifier folds are uncontrolled here exactly as in ops-grammar; see that archive's `uncontrolled` field.
run_weakening_filter's default moved to false on 2026-08-20, after this campaign. Both arms state run_weakening = false explicitly in their emitted configs, so nothing here is silently reinterpreted.
